A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TOPS research, with matching methods and retained main results. The complete text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original reasoning-effort experiments, erroneous-round analysis, and TOPS self-improvement results on GSM8K, MATH500 and AIME2024, including Figures 3–5 and Table 2.

after.justification: v2 retains these experiments and adds original masking, filtering, LLaMA self-improvement and general-reasoning results, including Figure 5 and Tables 4, 9 and 10.

M1.justification: TOPS retains format imitation, reasoning-effort-conditioned generation, shortest-correct-response selection and supervised self-improvement. The iterative SFT and DPO procedures also remain unchanged. New loss-masking and filtering experiments are diagnostic variants, not revisions to the proposed TOPS procedure.

E1.justification: v1's empirical coverage is mathematical reasoning. v2 adds WebInstruct-verified data for general-reasoning training and self-improvement, with evaluation on MMLU-Pro and GPQA-Diamond in Appendix J. This substantially extends task coverage while retaining the mathematical datasets.

E2.justification: Figure 1 adds DeepSeek-R1 and DeepSeek-V3-0324 to the preliminary model comparison, and Appendix H evaluates QwQ-32B alongside QwQ-32B-Preview. The main TOPS comparator set remains unchanged: QwQ-32B-Preview, STILL-2-32B, Sky-T1-32B-Preview, Random and the base model.

E3.justification: v2 introduces controlled masked-loss and filtered-data experiments, an answer-diversity metric, full TOPS evaluation on LLaMA3.1-8B, and a Qwen2.5-7B general-reasoning setup. Appendix H specifies a 32K limit for the newly evaluated QwQ-32B. These are substantial added protocols; the retained main experiments' hyperparameters and decoding settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds interventions testing the effect of erroneous training steps through loss masking and solution filtering. It also adds answer-consistency analysis, MATH500 difficulty breakdowns, prompt-following and direct-prompting analyses, and an o1-mini token-estimation check. These substantially extend v1's reasoning-effort and erroneous-round analyses.

E5.justification: v1 reports five-seed averages without dispersion. v2 adds accuracy standard deviations across the main LLaMA and Qwen comparisons in Appendix K, including retained results, substantially expanding uncertainty reporting. The five-seed count is unchanged; Appendix J separately specifies one sample per prompt for the new general-reasoning evaluations.

E6.justification: Every numerical row in v1 Table 2 is retained in v2 Table 3, but substantial new results appear elsewhere. For example, LLaMA TOPS-SFT obtains 61.28% on MATH500 versus Random-SFT's 60.52% (Table 4), while TOPS-General obtains 56.50% on MMLU-Pro and 38.38% on GPQA-Diamond (Table 10). These are newly reported experiments, not improvements over revised v1 scores.

T1.justification: The thinking-optimal-response definition, optimization objectives and token-estimation formula are retained. Equation 2 clarifies conditional-distribution notation without changing the described sampling procedure. No substantive mathematical assumptions, derivations or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central claims that excessive CoT scaling can harm accuracy, optimal effort depends on task difficulty, and TOPS improves efficiency and effectiveness. Calling QwQ-32B-Preview the teacher in the revised abstract clarifies an already documented relationship.

C2.justification: v2 adds an answer-consistency interpretation and explains why removing erroneous solutions helps easier tasks but can sacrifice useful correction behavior on harder tasks, motivating step masking. Section 7 newly discusses the predominantly mathematical and SFT scope and proposes an explicitly untested extension to RL. These substantially expand the interpretation and applicability discussion.

D1.justification: v2 newly states that code, data and models are available and supplies a project repository reference, materially extending reproducibility information. Appendix E also discloses training hardware, including four or eight H100 80GB GPUs depending on stage, and four A100 80GB GPUs for evaluation. Existing hyperparameters and prompts are largely retained or relocated.

R1.justification: v2 adds seven references, including DeepSeek-V3, QwQ-32B, General-Reasoner, MMLU-Pro, Star-R1, DeepCritic and TinyR1. These update experimental context and related research, while the related-work taxonomy and positioning against efficiency-focused overthinking studies remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence are preserved. v2 makes localized wording and terminology corrections, relocates prompts, training details and the impact statement, and adds a LLaMA results subsection, limitations and appendix sections. The retained narrative is not extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: v2 adds numerous diagnostic, model-comparison, general-reasoning and uncertainty tables plus a loss-masking plot. Figure 1 gains model points and revised axis ranges; the erroneous-round plot gains a ratio curve and secondary axis. The original prompt panel moves to Figure 7, while the main results table is preserved as Table 3.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens v1's largely correlational explanation of harmful training errors with masking and filtering interventions, and tests TOPS beyond its original backbone and mathematical tasks. Standard deviations, explicit limitations and artifact-access information further improve evidential transparency and reproducibility. General-reasoning evaluations remain single-sample and RL applicability remains speculative, but these limits do not outweigh the substantial gains in validation.
